newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares down at noon in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares down at noon in cautious trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices fell during the morning session on Thursday, due to worries that securities regulators would enact new anti-speculation policies, brokers said.
But turnover was thin as investors took a wait-and-see attitude, they said.
The foreign currency B share index slipped 2.14 points or 1.35 percent to 156.66 on turnover of HK$19 million.
The domestic currency A share index lost 6.82 points or 1.44 percent to 467.35 on turnover of 3.3 billion yuan.
"Investors were a bit cautious in the morning, and buying interest was weak as concerns over possible new crackdown measures dominated the market," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Brokers said they expected the bearish mood to extend into the afternoon trading session.
On the B share market, textile concern Shenzhen Victor Onward was the worst performer, falling HK$0.22 or 8.87 percent to HK$2.26 due to pessimism over the company's prospects, brokers said.
On the A share market, aluminum processor Jiaozuo Wanfang was the biggest loser, dipping 0.58 yuan or 5.01 percent to 11.00 yuan.
